bug_semantics: Scriban's recursive-descent expression parser counts nesting in EnterExpression() and, when ExpressionDepthLimit is exceeded, only LogError()s a non-fatal message and sets _isExpressionDepthLimitReached (used solely to dedupe that message). Parsing does not throw, return a sentinel, or unwind. Deeply nested parentheses, array initializers, object initializers, or unary operators therefore keep descending until the native thread stack is exhausted, raising an uncatchable StackOverflowException that kills the host process. Template.Parse, Template.ParseLiquid, and runtime object.eval / object.eval_template share this parser. Versions 6.6.0-7.2.0 ship a default limit of 250 that does not actually halt descent; pre-6.6.0 had the same non-enforcing helper with a null default (unbounded). CWE-674 DoS.
flaw_origin: The smallest first write of the non-enforcing expression-depth guard is e0f646d899e60c8b88f01ebae6f998fc49116e09 (2017-11-03, Alexandre Mutel). That commit introduced ExpressionDepthLimit (renamed from StatementDepthLimit), _expressionDepth, _isExpressionDepthLimitReached, EnterExpression() that increments depth then LogError()s without stopping, and the ParseExpression() call that records expressionDepthBeforeEntering then continues recursive descent. Immediate parent 5f039d2d2bb86e680a8c06d7cc739f26d7324705 still has StatementDepthLimit on the block parser and has no EnterExpression, _expressionDepth, or ExpressionDepthLimit on Parser.cs / Parser.Expressions.cs / ParserOptions.cs. Later commits are not the BIC: a6fe6074199e5c04f4d29dc8d8e652b24d33e3e4 only set the property default to 250 (the 6.6.0 advertised guard); b5ac4bf30459fdc76964e3f751e16f7e96079ea7 and e5f6950f1dd24b001a20f5f17f29f6edc4fb1d29 only retargeted how that default is applied; f55280a09575e577fcf7f5629007e0814594e3ac wrapped ParseArrayInitializer in the same non-stopping helper; 234d3f400936ae8bf1ae114bc39ad930f1b06d58 is a file split. Direct fix 8fdbd687bbe8f00085c4c4c5b2b3b8d529933949 makes the limit fatal (FatalParserException plus EnsureSufficientExecutionStack) and is in 7.2.1, not 7.2.0.
